artifacts.summary: Decisions with reasons and rejected alternatives for the twelve open questions (a)-(l), two needs-user-ruling items listed first, and the edit lists for the three records and three review files.

user_decision.question: What does 'default' mean for proof-mode adoption (M12), given that proofs under FormalSystem/Theorems/ cannot be written in the mode?
options: A+B — library registration requires a proof-mode script or a recorded failure class, and new Examples/ and case-study modules are written in the mode; Theorems/ exempt by layering; contingent on a GO at gate one
B only — library registration requires a script or a failure class; examples and case studies stay free
C — the mode stays optional outside the library's sweeps (requires rewriting M12's done-when)
user_decision.recommended: A+B — library registration requires a proof-mode script or a recorded failure class, and new Examples/ and case-study modules are written in the mode; Theorems/ exempt by layering; contingent on a GO at gate one

memory_candidates.content: In BimodalLogic, FormalSystem/Semantics/ is layer 1 and FormalSystem/Theorems/ is layer 2 (LAYERS in scripts/measure-refactor-partitions.py; ORGANISATION.md). Text saying Semantics is layer 2 is wrong. A module placed under Semantics/ can import only layers 0-1, so anything it shares with Automation/ (layer 3) must live at layer 0 or 1, e.g. FormalSystem/Tactic/.

Collaborator PR heads in BimodalLogic are available as local refs pr/N-head; a module's import closure on a PR can be computed with git ls-tree and git show without checking out or building the branch.

A Lean class indexed by an operator function (class C (box : L -> L)) admits two instances on one formula type and resolves at the constant and at its eta-expansion, but fails to resolve when the operator is presented through a def. A structure with the operator as a field has no such failure. TM box, TM-plus box and the stability operator have three different S5 axiom bases, so a shared S5 statement must take theorems, not axioms, as fields.
